title: Benchmarking Federated Learning in Edge Computing Environments: A Systematic Review and Performance Evaluation
venue: Journal of Advances in Information Technology
tldr: Systematic review benchmarking five federated learning algorithms across four datasets reveals SCAFFOLD achieves highest accuracy (0.90) while FedAvg excels in communication and energy efficiency for edge computing.
problem_and_motivation: Federated learning faces critical challenges in edge computing environments, including data heterogeneity, energy limitations, and communication overhead, yet no comprehensive review systematically categorizes and benchmarks these techniques against practical performance metrics relevant to edge scenarios.
approach: Conducted a systematic literature review following PRISMA and SALSA guidelines, screening 602 articles down to 308 for full-text analysis from six major academic databases.
Classified federated learning techniques into a four-dimensional taxonomy: optimization strategies, communication efficiency, privacy enhancements, and system architecture.

Benchmarked five leading algorithms (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedNova, FedAvg+DP) using standardized performance indicators including accuracy, convergence time, communication overhead, energy consumption, and non-IID robustness.
Synthesized comparative results from MNIST, CIFAR-10, FEMNIST, and Shakespeare datasets to evaluate algorithm suitability across edge computing deployment scenarios.
findings: SCAFFOLD achieves the highest accuracy (84.7%) and convergence speed (95 rounds) among all benchmarked algorithms.
SCAFFOLD achieves highest non-IID robustness (0.90) and accuracy (0.90) in normalized evaluation.
FedAvg demonstrates superior communication efficiency (0.85) and energy use (0.75) for constrained edge devices.
Privacy-enhanced FedAvg+DP shows 74.1% accuracy and 135 rounds convergence, indicating significant privacy-utility trade-off.
num: 602 articles screened, 308 retained for full-text review across six academic databases.
FEMNIST (3400 clients) and Shakespeare (1126 clients) identified as most representative of real-world non-IID conditions.
SecureFed achieves 79.8% accuracy with high privacy but requires 58 MB/round communication overhead.

definitions.definition: Federated Learning: a decentralized machine learning approach where multiple clients collaboratively train a shared global model without sharing raw data.
Non-Independent and Identically Distributed: data distributions across clients that are statistically heterogeneous due to differing user behaviors.
Differential Privacy: a privacy mechanism that adds calibrated noise to local updates or aggregations to prevent re-identification of individual data points.
Secure Multiparty Computation: enables multiple parties to jointly compute functions without revealing their individual inputs.
Homomorphic Encryption: allows computations to be performed directly on encrypted data while preserving privacy during processing.
Internet of Things: network of interconnected physical devices that collect and exchange data.
A decentralized computing paradigm that processes data at or near the source of data generation rather than relying on centralized cloud servers.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides a comprehensive four-dimensional taxonomy of federated learning techniques adapted for edge computing, covering optimization strategies, communication efficiency, privacy enhancements, and system architectures. It presents a systematic benchmarking of five leading FL algorithms (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedNova, FedAvg+DP) across standardized performance metrics and datasets, revealing critical trade-offs between accuracy, convergence speed, communication overhead, energy consumption, and privacy. The review identifies six persistent open challenges—data heterogeneity, client reliability, communication overhead, energy efficiency, privacy-security, and benchmarking reproducibility—and proposes a structured research agenda spanning lightweight algorithms, adaptive learning, multi-tier architectures, and standardized real-world testbeds.
directly_justifies: SCAFFOLD achieves the highest accuracy (0.90) and non-IID robustness (0.90) among benchmarked algorithms.
FedAvg demonstrates superior communication efficiency (0.85) and energy use (0.75) for constrained edge devices.
Privacy-enhanced FedAvg+DP lags in convergence and accuracy, indicating a significant performance-privacy trade-off.
FEMNIST (3400 clients) and Shakespeare (1126 clients) are most representative of real-world non-IID conditions.
Six core challenge areas persist: data heterogeneity, client reliability, communication overhead, energy efficiency, privacy, and benchmarking.
Balancing personalization with global generalization remains an unsolved open problem in federated learning.
limits: Simulation-based evaluations simplify real-world edge conditions, potentially overestimating performance metrics.
No new empirical experiments were conducted; results are synthesized from existing independent studies.
Cross-study comparisons are limited by heterogeneous experimental configurations and dataset partitioning schemes.
Focuses primarily on horizontal FL, leaving vertical FL and federated transfer learning largely unbenchmarked.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned for citeable claims. Domain 14 (ML System Design) was flagged as highly relevant, with codes 14.B (ML Model Serving and Deployment, high) and 14.C (On-Device vs. Server Inference, high) directly applicable to the paper's taxonomy of FL architectures and algorithm benchmarking. Domain 10 (Privacy) was flagged as medium-relevant via 10.A, as the paper provides a comprehensive review of differential privacy, SMPC, and homomorphic encryption. Domain 9 (Mobile/Offline Design) was flagged as medium via 9.C due to discussion of intermittent connectivity, client reliability, and decentralized training characteristics. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as low via 6.A, as FL optimization and convergence topics are tangentially applicable to predictive finance. Domain 14.A (Synthetic Data Generation) and 10.B (User Trust) were assigned contextual relevance, as they appear in the paper's discussion of benchmarking datasets and privacy guarantees but not in a personal finance framing. Domains 1-5 (Demographics, Financial Structure/Behavior, Expense Categorization, Existing PF Systems, Behavioral Profiles), Domain 7 (Budgeting Strategies), Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection), Domain 11 (Engagement/Retention), Domain 12 (Evaluation Frameworks for PF Systems), and Domain 13 (Savings/Debt Management) were all considered and rejected as the paper does not address personal finance systems, budgeting, financial behavior, or related application domains. The paper is fundamentally a systematic review of federated learning in edge computing, not a personal finance contribution.

limitations: Simulation-based evaluations simplify real-world edge conditions including network instability, hardware heterogeneity, and mobility. [unacknowledged]
No new empirical experiments conducted; findings are synthesized from heterogeneous independent studies with varying configurations.
Cross-study comparison limited by inconsistent dataset partitioning, hardware platforms, and privacy budget configurations.
Focuses primarily on horizontal FL, leaving vertical FL and federated transfer learning largely unbenchmarked due to scarce standardized benchmarks.
Energy consumption values are normalized across disparate hardware platforms rather than measured on a single reference system.
Static differential privacy configurations used in benchmarking do not represent advanced adaptive privacy mechanisms.
remember_this: SCAFFOLD achieves highest accuracy (84.7%) and fastest convergence (95 rounds) among benchmarked FL algorithms.
Privacy-enhanced FedAvg+DP shows significant accuracy and convergence penalties compared to non-private FedAvg.
Six core challenge areas persist: data heterogeneity, client reliability, communication, energy, privacy, and benchmarking.
FEMNIST and Shakespeare are most representative benchmarking datasets for real-world non-IID edge conditions.
Adaptive FL frameworks adjusting to device context are essential for dynamic edge environments.
